body:
## Context

In M5 (#119, PR #137, and #121, PR #142), an operator can settle an unknown external operation without supplying a value:

- **Resolve as succeeded.** The operation's address stays consumed. A later call there throws `operation-resolved` and sends nothing, so the member fails until an operator abandons the operation.
- **Abandon.** Frees the address and explicitly authorizes a possible second effect.

This is recorded in RUN-012 and in `docs/validation/m5-2026-10-01.md` as a limit.

## Deferred work

Resolution that carries a result value was deferred to the M6 operator surface. It would let an operator supply the provider's response for an unknown operation, so the step completes without a second effect.

This issue records the deferral only. Design and scheduling belong to M6 planning. The value would be subject to the event-privacy rules, so it would never enter events or diagnostics.
title: Operator resolution of an unknown operation that carries a result value (deferred from M5)

Specified-but-missing target, P2. **Leave unlabelled; not implementation-ready until owner decisions below are recorded.** RUN-006–008 in `docs/spec/operations.md` govern the capability; CLI-004 consumes it. M6 inspection needs this support, while the milestone does not independently name every preview mechanism. This is not a regression against bounded M5 acceptance.

## Consumer need and evidence

An operator needs the latest available value with its freshness/error state while deciding whether to continue. A failed refresh must preserve a prior value visibly as stale; no-prior failure must remain distinguishable from successful undefined/zero/empty data. Observation must never initiate refresh work.

The synthetic histogram control publishes once, fails the next authorized refresh, then reads the saved exact reference 1,000 times without another fetch (fetch count stays 2). Exact reads preserve immutable author data. Complete generated run/observer surface inspection finds no latest-value envelope, subscription lifetime or throttle/coalescing contract. Lifecycle events and exact-reference reads are useful existing controls; they do not deliver this target.

## Pinned reproduction

From a clean checkout of `0683c2ed73934d10f9b5a1ad9e0dd9e3d1a88d4f`, on branch `gap-hunt-durability`, with Node 24.x/npm, registry access and the native prebuild/toolchain prerequisites:

```sh
bash scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/verify-preview.sh
```

The runner performs `npm ci`, builds package declarations and runs valid controls. Successful diagnostic completion exits 0: it confirms the reviewed baseline surface and is **not** a behavioral regression test that becomes green after implementation. Write behavioral tests first once the owner selects the contract. [Runner and captured macOS log](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/0683c2ed73934d10f9b5a1ad9e0dd9e3d1a88d4f/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations) are pinned to that revision. The controls were executed on macOS Node24.22.1; the Node24.x patch-version guard is syntax-checked. This runner has not been verified on Linux; the separate owner Linux parity report covers earlier commits and different commands. No paid provider is called.

## Owner decisions

1. Select envelope discriminants and error/status retention across updates: how absence, stale/unverified value, accepted value and refresh error coexist, including successful undefined.
2. Select observation lifetime: run-owned observation versus an independently opened read-side lifetime; define attachment, disposal and aggregate replacement/removal. Disposal must not implicitly select execution cancellation.
3. Select optional throttle delivery details and clock ownership: periodic latest-state delivery under sustained arrivals, final trailing state, equal-data status changes and disposal boundary. No API spelling is prescribed.

## Conditional implementation acceptance

1. After decisions, write tests first for failed refresh with/without prior data, successful undefined/zero/empty values and freshness changes with equal author data. A verified consumer reports refresh failure; stale preview never becomes accepted success.
2. Negative controls make dispatch, source refresh, claim renewal and writes fail if attempted; repeated observation succeeds without invoking them. Existing exact-reference reads keep their current meaning.
3. Controlled-clock sustained arrivals produce periodic latest states and a final coalesced state, with the selected disposal behavior. Member updates replace prior contributions, established removals disappear, and selected-field observation does not load unrelated large payloads.

Scope: the observation boundary with Materialization and its read-side integration. Coordinate ownership with the CLI issue; CLI depends on this contract. M7 scale optimization, automatic refresh/retry, terminal/GUI toolkit and a general incremental-query engine are excluded.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (gpt-6.1-sol), operating for Mike North, authored the evidence fixtures and this issue draft; no target implementation is claimed.
Agent assistance: Worker ran synthetic controls and declaration diagnostics. Supervising Codex reviewed the owning contracts, independently reran the controls/diagnostic, checked live issue/PR/label state, and filed this gap. Owner decisions remain open; no human implementation/review is claimed.

Governing source: [operations contract](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/operations.md). No fix PR is included.

Blocking implementation dependency: the owner decisions above. No prerequisite issue must be fixed before design work; this is not permission to implement an unsettled author contract.

A provider reports remaining quota 93 then 90 in one account pool/reset window while requests consume 2 then 3 units. Consumers need state 90 alongside consumption 5, with other pools/windows separate and missing state visible. Recording reset time must not schedule a retry.

The valid current control reports additive consumption 2 + 3 and observes 5. ## Consumer need and evidence

A separate process must inspect retained values, attempts, acceptance/dependency evidence, errors, waits and observed usage without loading current analysis callbacks or starting work. Status must distinguish verification/reuse/execution, waiting, mixed outcomes and incomplete discovery honestly.

The raw installed-command discovery attempt reports `could not determine executable to run`; every package/root manifest lacks bin. The complete alpha workspace surface has run/close/logicalStore, with read/check/recover/usage/operation inspection inside a run requiring authoring/composition. body:
**Medium authoring/DX correctness.** A supported asynchronous source check works at runtime but is rejected by the generated private-alpha authoring declarations.

## Consumer contract and classification

Current source authoring should permit a check/retrieval callback to await work before returning its trusted fresh/retain outcome. `docs/spec/execution.md` REUSE-004 describes a conditional request confirming unchanged data and retaining the previous exact snapshot, with the work recorded separately. M5 operational work is scoped to the invocation lifetime. This need exists for an ordinary source today and does not depend on future M7 pagination.

This is a scoped **declaration gap**: strict generated-alpha TypeScript rejects `async ({ outcome }) => outcome.fresh<IValue>({ value: 1 })` and async conditional retain, although JavaScript runtime controls execute those outcomes correctly. No synchronous-source boundary was found in active M3/M4/M5 plans. Their synchronous restrictions concern SQLite/selected materialization getters. The sync/async implementation-choice sentence at execution.md:187 refers to finality hooks; it does not require source check/retrieval to be synchronous.

## Minimal reproduction and exact boundary

`async-source.ts` imports only the facade API with the required generated owner-declaration mappings. Matching synchronous fresh/retain controls compile. Four async callbacks fail with **TS2322**: direct source fresh/retain and template-member source fresh/retain. Every payload is the supported object `{ value: 1 }`; no cast, suppression or weakened compiler setting is used.

The restrictive signatures are `packages/definition/src/declaration.ts:230` (`ISourceOptions.run`) and `packages/definition/src/template.ts:90` (`ITemplateSourceOptions.run`), both returning only `IApply<TFamily['outcomes'], TResult>`. Resolution's family maps that directly to `ISourceOutcome<TResult>` (`packages/resolution/src/family.ts:64`). Runtime `callSource` at `resolution.ts:1120` returns captured asynchronous invocation completion. Runtime evidence is direct sources only; no template-runtime parity claim is inferred from it.

JavaScript/Jest controls pass **2/2**: async fresh publishes; a separate-process async check retains the exact earlier reference; rejection after an await propagates as failure. An initial harness descriptor omitted required scope/role and failed before callbacks; it was corrected before this evidence. No product failure is inferred from that harness mistake.

True-negative tsd controls pass: forged/wrong outcome envelope, scalar supplied to explicitly object-shaped `IValue`, and promised scalar outcome supplied to an object-shaped source remain rejected. This does **not** establish a general scalar-root policy: #156 owns the existing generic scalar-root acceptance mismatch. Async repair must neither expand roots nor claim to fix #156.

## Portable red-to-green command

From a clean checkout of `gap-hunt-dx` at [`faaa87426c565452d24cb128a1cfb4df3bc86405`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/faaa87426c565452d24cb128a1cfb4df3bc86405), run:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/consumer-dx/repro-async-source.mjs
```

Node 24.x; default clean `npm ci` and package build, strict generated-declaration compiler check, tsd negatives, type-aware lint and isolated Jest. On this baseline the compiler reports exactly four TS2322 errors; the runner still executes the independent lint/type-negative/runtime controls, then exits **2**. After a correct declaration repair, compilation succeeds and the same command exits **0**. Unexpected compiler diagnostics stop the replay. `GAP_HUNT_REUSE_BUILD=1` explicitly skips installation/build during development.

Captured complete baseline replay: `logs/async-source-replay.log`. It reused fresh generated packages. The analogous M7 runner's **default** clean install/build was separately verified in a detached e6fc3de checkout: `logs/m7-clean-bootstrap.log` (3/3 snapshot controls). Those M7 controls are not evidence for this async-source acceptance.

## Numbered acceptance criteria / contained pickup

1. Direct source fresh and retain callbacks support both synchronous trusted outcomes and asynchronously completed trusted outcomes under strict generated-alpha declarations. The unchanged `async-source.ts` direct-source cases must compile; no casts, `any`, `unknown` result widening, suppression or `skipLibCheck` workaround.
2. Template-member source fresh/retain supports the same completion semantics, preserving precise previous/member/payload types. The unchanged two template cases must compile. Keep synchronous existing callbacks source compatible.
3. Wrong result shape, wrong/forged control envelope and Promise of the wrong declared result remain rejected by tsd. A Promise must not erase the source result type or mint trust. Supported result roots remain governed by current runtime constraints and #156; this issue does not add scalar roots.
4. Runtime controls prove awaited fresh publication and awaited explicit retention after restart preserving the exact previous reference. Fresh equal object data must still produce a distinct publication, and retaining without an eligible previous carrier must remain rejected. Add missing negative controls before an implementation change if not already covered by owner tests.
5. Rejection after await must fail the source check without successful publication/acceptance; a previously completed result remains historically readable. Preserve current admission, active execution lifetime, cancellation and source-policy ordering. Do not infer that a Promise permits work to escape supervision.
6. Cover template-member runtime parity for the selected async cases before calling both signatures closed. Preserve trusted source outcome handling and consumed read capture across await; do not make memo/output/materialization contracts more permissive to fix callback typing.
7. Rebuild generated declarations/API reports and run focused Jest, tsd, strict compiler and type-aware lint checks. The portable command above must become green as written; do not invert expected errors to make the original gap a passing test.

Owners: Definition owns direct/template callback contracts; Resolution owns its outcome family and execution/capture semantics; facade generated declarations must expose the corrected precision. Dependencies: existing source outcome/retention contracts only. #156 is related separate root policy; no dependency on M7, #152 result-bearing operator settlement or new adapters. No new public API spelling, host or persistence authority is prescribed.

## Scope, readiness and attribution

Pickup-ready; no blocking production dependency is known. Scope is direct and template source callback declarations, their precise generated facade contracts, and focused tests/docs. Out of scope: scalar-root support, M7 streaming/pagination, changes to persistence or provider protocols, new hosts, paid/live provider execution, release-tier promotion, publication or release automation. Coordinate any overlapping signature edits with #156 without coupling this fix to that issue.

Implementer: Codex gap-hunt workers (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North, produced the compiler and runtime evidence.
Agent assistance: Supervising Codex checked the contract boundary, independently executed the four-error compiler reproduction with passing tsd/lint and two Jest runtime controls, rechecked live issues/PRs/labels, and filed the issue. No human implementation or review is claimed.
title: Allow asynchronous fresh and retain callbacks in generated source declarations

body:
## Problem and severity

**Low documentation/DX.** Current canonical-location comments imply that every name for one file shares an identity. The implementation resolves path spellings and symbolic links, but distinct hard-linked names remain distinct. Author-facing durable-store guidance does not explain this limit or SQLite's journal/WAL naming hazard.

## Consumer need and actual contract

An author choosing the location of a project-private durable workspace needs to know which filesystem names are interchangeable before opening a SQLite WAL store. `canonicalNodeLocation` provides an **absolute real path** for an existing local file: relative/absolute spellings, redundant segments and symbolic links resolve to the same canonical path. Different hard-linked names are distinct canonical paths. Authors must not concurrently access one SQLite WAL database through those different hard-linked names; associated journal/WAL names make that unsafe. This is documentation of the existing path API and backend limit, not a proposal to normalize inodes or support hard links.

Current TSDoc overstates its scope: `packages/machine-node/src/index.ts` says “two spellings of one file compare equal”; `packages/core/src/workspace.ts` says “however the caller spelled its location”. The supported symbolic/path scope is narrower. `canonicalNodeLocation` is project-private alpha and implemented by `realpathSync.native` in Node Machine. Host identity mechanics remain Machine-owned; writer/fencing/publication policy stays History/Supervision-owned. No implementation change is needed for this pickup.

Live duplicate check: identity-enforced `gh issue list --state all --search 'hard link'` plus the complete current open issue title list found no existing dedicated alias-boundary issue. Snapshots: `hardlink-queue-live.json` and `store-location-open-queue.json`. #158 concerns native installation/linker setup; #138 concerns busy-contention typing; #161 covers broad current-checkout documentation. Coordinate nearby native/current-checkout prose without expanding this narrow issue into those tasks. No issue was filed or edited by this worker.

## Governing evidence

- API/source: `packages/machine-node/src/index.ts:57–65`, `src/node/location.ts`; core workspace canonical identity comment near `const store = canonicalNodeLocation(options.location)`.
- Positive runtime: existing Machine `test/node-location.test.ts` covers canonical symbolic/redundant paths, distinct files and missing-file refusal. The original symbolic-file alias probe also observes one fenced writer and exact shared reference reads.
- Provisional negative observation: original `packages/core/test/gap-hunt-portability-alias.test.ts` seeded a disposable database, created another hard link, opened both pathnames and failed at first writer acquisition with raw `SqliteError: disk I/O error`. Linux aarch64 Node24.13.0/26.12.1 at `bfb1cc3` report the failure too. No competing ownership grant, stale publication, corruption or extended SQLite I/O cause was established. Existing logs suffice; **do not rerun or adopt that intentionally red support expectation as an acceptance requirement**.
- [SQLite official §2.6](https://sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html#_multiple_links_to_the_same_file) explains different database names can use different rollback-journal/WAL names. Local source excerpt/provenance is `sqlite-multiple-links-source.json`; detailed review is `LINUX-ISSUES-HARDLINK-AUDIT.md`.

PUB-002 continues to govern ownership mutations but this observation is not a PUB-002 violation. There is no new runtime rejection/error-class requirement. Previously calling the topology simply “unsupported” was shorthand; this pickup makes the author guidance explicit without claiming an earlier normative prohibition.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. State the actual canonical API boundary in native/store-location author guidance: absolute and relative paths, redundant segments and symbolic links are supported canonical spellings of an existing local store; distinct hard-linked names do not become one canonical identity. Missing-file behavior remains unchanged.
2. State the practical SQLite restriction: authors must not concurrently open the same WAL database through different hard-linked names. Explain the journal/WAL sidecar naming reason and link official SQLite guidance. Do not imply symbolic links share the hard-link limitation; preserve the existing selected symbolic canonicalization positives.
3. Make the guidance directly discoverable from root README, facade README and contribution example README. They may state it or directly link one shared local native/storage guide; no prescribed heading, exact prose or new guide filename is required. Keep project-private alpha usage separate from the public memory Store API.
4. Narrow the two owning comments (`canonicalNodeLocation` TSDoc and core's canonical store key comment) to supported path/symbolic normalization, explicitly distinguishing hard-linked names. Remove their unqualified “two spellings of one file compare equal” / “however the caller spelled” implications. Preserve durable semantic commentary and ownership boundaries.
5. Before documentation edits, run the supplied one-command check and observe the intended five missing-guidance/comment failures with canonical runtime positives passing. After edits, the same command must pass. The checker verifies prose concept/link coverage and obsolete wording removal; substantive review checks whether the explanation is correct. It is not runtime proof of hard-link topology behavior.
6. Preserve runtime/API/dependency behavior and the existing supported-path tests. No runtime rejection/error class, inode normalization, hard-link interoperability, driver/engine change, package publication, release automation, global toolchain change or all-SQLite-I/O translation belongs in this task. Do not turn the historic I/O observation into a corruption, Linux native-install or fencing claim.

## Clean one-command acceptance

Reproduction branch: `gap-hunt-durability`, pinned commit [`275124b32fbd1b960cf8fa46b5e341b51dfdb38e`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/275124b32fbd1b960cf8fa46b5e341b51dfdb38e). Both scripts are committed at that revision. From its clean checkout, at the repository root:

```sh
bash scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/verify-store-location-docs.sh
```

The default command installs locked dependencies, builds generated owner/facade packages needed by strict consumers, typechecks Machine Node and core, compiles Machine tests, syntax-checks the new dependency-free documentation checker, runs only the existing canonical-location 3-test suite, then runs 5 documentation assertions. It does not invoke the hard-link probe, native rebuild diagnostic, full `npm test`, paid provider or GitHub write. Standard npm/native-toolchain prerequisites apply if dependencies need source compilation. Build/install trust and toolchain policy remain #157/#158's separate scope. `GAP_HUNT_REUSE_BUILD=1` skips install/build only for a known prepared checkout and is not fresh-bootstrap evidence.

The five docs assertions permit a directly linked shared guide and check concepts (supported path forms, distinct hard-linked names, unsafe concurrent WAL/journal use) rather than exact replacement prose. All assertions are evidence helpers under scratch; an implementer may carry/graduate them as appropriate without changing package runtime behavior or broadening the task.

Independent supervisor verification: the exact pinned commit `275124b` was checked out into a new `gap-hunt-review-location-docs` worktree with no installed dependencies. The unchanged default command installed/built successfully, passed canonical runtime tests **3/3**, then failed the intended documentation checks **0/5** with exit1. The checkout remained git-clean. This confirms the committed one-command starting point, without copying fixture files into the checkout. macOS arm64 Node24.22.1 only.

## Scope and dependencies

Pickup-ready for documentation and comment corrections only. Blocking dependencies: none. Coordinate adjacent native guidance with #157/#158; their package-manager and linker tasks are not prerequisites. #138 contention typing and the merged #161 package map are separate. Queue after correctness work and other higher-priority needs. Workflow labels remain the supervisor's responsibility.

## Baseline result and attribution

Prepared-checkout command: strict Machine/core checks and existing canonical 3/3 pass; docs 0/5, with expected failures naming each of the three entrypoints and two overbroad comments (`store-location-docs-red.log`). Default clean-bootstrap verification in a new detached checkout at `c5a3f273ed23acd75a833cbf0c6565e196e29e37` on macOS arm64, Node v24.22.1, installed 614 locked packages, completed the generated-package build and strict compilation, passed the canonical tests 3/3, then failed exactly the five documentation assertions (exit 1). Evidence: `store-location-docs-clean-red.log` and `store-location-docs-clean-context.json`. The empty `cleanAfter` field records tracked checkout cleanliness after execution; isolation before execution follows from creating the detached checkout and copying only the two new scratch helper scripts. No implementation docs/comments have been changed in this evidence branch.

Implementer: Codex worker (gpt-6.1-sol), operating for Mike North, authored the pickup and executable prose checks and inspected prior alias evidence. Agent assistance: supervising Codex reviewed the prior audit and narrowed this task to documentation; no human implementation/review, new Linux execution or GitHub mutation is claimed.

Evidence report and captured logs: [pickup directory](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/275124b32fbd1b960cf8fa46b5e341b51dfdb38e/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations). The supplied Linux results cover the historical alias observation; this new documentation runner has not run on Linux.
